d: When a teenage couple are found dead in Montana in 1956, detectives suspect an infamous gangster might be responsible. Unfortunately it will take 65 years and new breakthroughs in technology to find the true culprit.
In 2018, a 79-year-old woman in Utah was sexually assaulted after a man broke into her home. It was the work of genetic genealogy that was able to immediately identify the man responsible.
In 1997, a woman is attacked on her route home; a suspect is arrested over 20 years later with the help of a genetic genealogical search.
In 1974, a 5-year-old girl disappears while walking to her friend's house; after 46 years, detectives are able to put the case to rest using modern DNA technology.
Ricky Davis was convicted of the 1985 murder of a woman but always maintained his innocence. It took 18 years before re-examined DNA evidence proved him right.
Detectives work for decades to push to find the identity of the remains of two women and find their killer.
A woman takes a genealogy test to learn what happened to her estranged mother and is shocked to learn her DNA helped law enforcement identify a Jane Doe that remained a mystery for decades.
In 1981 a young woman is found murdered on the side of the road. The identity of her killer remains a mystery for decades until law enforcement can utilise genetic genealogy to crack the case.
In 1995, a masked man commits multiple sexual assaults at knife-point. It ends up taking over twenty years for this serial rapist to be identified and then to be brought to justice.
In Alexandria, Va. in 2016, a young female lifeguard is raped while working at a local pool; police soon learn of a similar incident in Fairfax. Va. two years previously.

st: The Hunt for Precious Jane Doe
d: In 1977, the body of a young woman is found covered in flies and maggots. Police officers fail to identify the victim until they utilize revolutionary technology which breaks open the case.
In 1968, a 60-year-old is brutally raped and killed inside the walls of her own home. A devastating flood halts the police investigation until ground-breaking science offers new hope.
In 1998, a 12-year-old girl and a 38-year-old woman are found raped and murdered. The case goes cold for over a decade until genetic genealogy uncovers the perpetrator.
In 1976, a young woman is found dead at a military base in Orange County, California. Using forensic genealogy, experts break open the 40-year-old cold case.

In 1987, in Ohio, the nude body of 17-year-old Barbara Blatnik is found face down on a rural road. She had been violently raped and strangled. Could this murder finally be solved with the help of genetic genealogy?
In 1988, Janet Tinsley reports her 8-year-old daughter April missing after she fails to return home. Three days later, a man out jogging makes a gruesome discovery in a nearby ditch.
In 1963, a man fishing finds the body of a toddler who had been wrapped in blankets and weighed down by iron moulds; it takes 57 years to learn the child's name.
In 1987, a man finds his wife brutally murdered on the kitchen floor.
17-year-old Carla Walker is with her boyfriend Rodney in his car when suddenly the door is ripped open by an unknown assailant. The man beats Rodney with a gun and drags Carla away screaming.
16-year-old high school student Kim Bryant is last seen outside a Dairy Queen restaurant. Three weeks later, her body is discovered by three teenage boys hiking on the outskirts of town.
